claim.pdf_says: A.4.8 FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling / A.4.9 Locale support and related functions / A.4.10 Object orientation / A.4.11 Report Writer — all printed in the same subsection style as A.4.1/A.4.2/A.4.12, subordinate to 'A.4 Optional language element list'.
claim.markdown_says:
## A.4.8 FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling
## A.4.9 Locale support and related functions
## A.4.10 Object orientation
## A.4.11 Report Writer   (vs. '### A.4.12 RESUME statement' on the following page)
claim.why_it_matters: Continuation of the same wrongly-levelled heading run: these four subsections of A.4 are emitted at level 2, the level of their parent A.4 and of the annex headings, while the immediately following A.4.12-A.4.14 are at level 3. Heading level is the only structure a markdown consumer has, so the annex outline is broken across this boundary.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED after independent render and source inspection; I tried to refute this on every available ground and could not.

(1) Not a misquote. Rendered specs/ISO_COBOL_2023.pdf page 1007 (printed folio 977) at 300dpi. The page carries, in order: 'A.4.8  FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling' (2 items), 'A.4.9  Locale support and related functions' (13 items), 'A.4.10  Object orientation' (3 items), 'A.4.11  Report Writer' (heading only, list continues on p1008). specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 39990/39997/40026/40035 emit exactly those four as '## '. Both sides quoted accurately.

(2) Not a 'missing text' claim that dissolves on reflow. All prose and every numbered item on page 1007 transcribes faithfully — I compared item-by-item and found zero content loss. So the finding rests entirely on heading level, and I evaluated it on that basis alone.

(3) Not merely cosmetic formatting. The transcription is internally self-contradicting at the same numbering depth. Full run in specs/ISO_COBOL.md: '## A.4 Optional language element list' (39846), then '### A.4.1' (39849) and '### A.4.2' (39864) correctly at level 3, then A.4.3 (39929), A.4.4 (39948), A.4.5 (39957), A.4.6 (39962), A.4.7 (39967), A.4.8 (39990), A.4.9 (39997), A.4.10 (40026), A.4.11 (40035) all at level 2, then '### A.4.12' (40103), '### A.4.13' (40108), '### A.4.14' (40115) back at level 3. Identical decimal depth is rendered at two different heading levels within one clause, which proves these are transcription errors rather than a deliberate style choice — the transcriber's own convention for an A.4.x subclause is '###'.

(4) The structural consequence is real, not theoretical. 'Annex A' (38875), 'A.2' (39466), 'A.3' (39672) and 'A.4' (39846) are all '##'. A '## A.4.8' therefore closes the A.4 subtree: any outline/TOC/section-slicing consumer reads A.4.8-A.4.11 as peers of Annex A and of A.4 itself, not as children of A.4. That inverts the containment the PDF asserts, so meaning is changed, not just presentation.

(5) I tested the strongest counter-argument — that the PDF supplies no level cue, leaving the transcriber free to choose. I measured glyph geometry on the renders (the ISO text layer is obfuscated, so font-metric extraction via PyMuPDF returned nothing and I fell back to pixel measurement). At 300dpi every heading in this annex shares one bold serif face at one size: ascender-band height 33-34px for descender-free titles ('A.4.1 General' 34, 'A.4.12 RESUME statement' 33, 'A.4.14 VALIDATE' 33) and 44-45px where descenders are present ('A.4 Optional language element list' 45, 'A.4.8 FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling' 45, 'A.4.9 Locale support and related functions' 44). So the PDF genuinely renders A.4 and A.4.x identically — but that defeats the counter-argument rather than supporting it, because it means the ONLY level signal the PDF carries is the decimal clause numbering, and ISO decimal numbering makes A.4.8 a subclause of A.4 by definition. The transcription honours that signal for A.4.1/A.4.2/A.4.12/A.4.13/A.4.14 and violates it for A.4.3-A.4.11.

One inaccuracy in the claim's PDF characterization, which I note but which does not weaken the finding: 'printed in the same subsection style as A.4.1/A.4.2/A.4.12' implies the PDF typographically distinguishes A.4 from its subclauses. It does not — parent A.4 is set in that same style too. Subordination comes from the numbering, not the type.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with two refinements to scope and labelling.

Scope: the mis-levelled run is not four headings but nine — A.4.3 Commit and Rollback (line 39929), A.4.4 Dynamic capacity tables (39948), A.4.5 DYNAMIC LENGTH elementary items (39957), A.4.6 Extended letters (39962), A.4.7 File sharing and record locking (39967), A.4.8 FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling (39990), A.4.9 Locale support and related functions (39997), A.4.10 Object orientation (40026), A.4.11 Report Writer (40035) — all emitted as '## ' in specs/ISO_COBOL.md. Page 1007 carries the last four of that run; the run begins on page 1006 and ends on page 1007. It is bracketed on both sides by correctly-levelled siblings: '### A.4.1'/'### A.4.2' before it and '### A.4.12'/'### A.4.13'/'### A.4.14' after it. Fix the whole A.4.3-A.4.11 span in one edit rather than page by page, or the outline stays broken on page 1006.

Labelling: kind should be 'wrong-heading-level', not 'missing-heading'. No heading text is missing — all four titles on page 1007 are present and spelled correctly, and every numbered item under them transcribes faithfully. The defect is purely that '##' should be '###'.

Corrected statement of the PDF side: ISO/IEC 1989:2023 page 1007 (folio 977) prints A.4.8, A.4.9, A.4.10 and A.4.11 in the identical bold serif face and size used for A.4 itself and for every other heading in Annex A — the PDF encodes no typographic level distinction anywhere in this annex. Subordination of A.4.8-A.4.11 to 'A.4 Optional language element list' is established solely by ISO decimal clause numbering, which the transcription honours for A.4.1/A.4.2 and A.4.12-A.4.14 but violates here.

Impact stands as claimed: because 'Annex A', 'A.2', 'A.3' and 'A.4' are themselves '##', a '## A.4.8' terminates the A.4 subtree and any outline-, TOC-, or section-slicing consumer reads these four subclauses as peers of Annex A instead of children of A.4.
